# A possible coefficient mechanism for the remaining frustum upper scalar

This is a research probe, NOT a proof for all dimensions. The exact all-dimensional obligation is scalar(10) in `candidate ce4a362fe44872e9`.

Use u in(0,1) for the top radius at the centered full section, and distinguish the mean radius p from its dth power p0:

    p=(d-1)(1-u^d)/[d(1-u^(d-1))], a=1-p,
    p0=p^d, t=u^d,
    e=u(1-u^(d-1))/[2(d-1)p^(d-1)(p-u)],
    h=(1+t-2p0)/[2(1+e)], kappa=p0+h,
    K=a p/[d u^(d-1)(p-u)^2],
    E=[p^(1-d)-(2-p)^(1-d)]/[2a(d-1)].

The endpoint identities give B-kappa=2eh and the moment multiplier beta=Kh. A sufficient unconditional inequality is

    F_d(u)=2eh-(kappa-2Kh)(E-1)>=0.                 (1)

When kappa-2Kh<=0 this is already immediate. In the other branch it is the outstanding scalar. No positive-part simplification or numerical observation is needed to state(1).

For exact integer d=2,...,9, symbolic cancellation of(1), orientation of its denominator to be positive on(0,1), and division of its numerator by(1-u)^3 produced a polynomial all of whose cumulative monomial coefficient sums were positive. Its Bernstein coefficients were also positive. For d>=3 the resulting polynomial degree was3d^2-2d-6. These finite observations do NOT prove the pattern for arbitrary d.

For d=2 the exact expression is

    F_2(u)=(u-1)^3(8u^2-u+1)/[4u(u-3)(3u+1)]>0.

A uniform coefficient-prefix certificate, if established, would be enough: if P(u)=sum c_i u^i and S_k=sum_(i<=k)c_i>=0, then

    P(u)=(1-u)sum_(k<degree P) S_k u^k+S_degree u^degree

is nonnegative on[0,1]. The outstanding task is to prove the necessary coefficient property from an explicit general expression, not to run more fixed dimensions.

Potential algebraic structure: let

    S=sum_(j=0)^(d-2)u^j, V=sum_(j=0)^(d-1)u^j,
    D=dS, A=(d-1)V,
    l=sum_(j=0)^(d-2)(j+1)u^j,
    r=sum_(j=0)^(d-2)(d-1-j)u^j.

Then p=A/D, a=(1-u)l/D, p-u=(1-u)r/D. The two positive coefficient sequences l and r are reversals of each other. Also

    e=u S D^d/[2(d-1)A^(d-1)r],
    K=l A/[d u^(d-1)(1-u)r^2].

These identities eliminate the implicit centered-slope root entirely. A convolution comparison or a dimension recurrence for the cleared numerator might prove the observed positivity, but none is asserted here.
